transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Start: 15:02 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Evan (Moonridge), Priya (CISO), Tom (ML Eng), Sara (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
Moonridge bank is evaluating hosting options for LLM inference across a set of regulated customer-facing workflows. Primary concerns: data residency, log retention policies, KMS/HSM key residency, PCI/HIPAA overlap for certain workloads, and ability to restrict telemetry. They asked about fallbacks, dedicated pools, and private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Next steps include paperwork, sample telemetry, and a short pilot.

Topics: residency routing, log visibility and redaction, KMS integration, regional fallbacks, SLAs for Dedicated, private control plane considerations, legal/EDR/forensics evidence handling.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time — should we do quick intros?
00:10 Evan: Yep Evan here, head of cloud platform at Moonridge, I run the infra for the product teams.
00:15 Priya: Priya Narang, CISO — mostly around compliance and regs.
00:19 Tom: Tom Adler, ML engineer, curious about latency and how we can keep data in-region.
00:23 Sara: Sara, counsel on privacy and contracts.
00:27 Maya: Awesome thanks, Jordan, want to give a quick technical framing?
00:31 Jordan: Sure. Quick overview: Redwood offers three hosting paths — hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private deployments, the latter either VPC-managed or on-prem. Each has different telemetry and control surfaces. Today we want to map Moonridge's regulated workloads to the right path and surface any gaps.
00:50 Priya: High level requirement — any data that touches customer PII for EU citizens must remain in EU jurisdictions, and logs that contain PII must either be redacted or never leave our control. Also we have HIPAA scoped data for a small product line and need BAA-level assurances.
01:10 Maya: Understood. For EU residency we can route requests to region-locked model endpoints; for PII we have prefix KV caching options and log scrubbing on the ingest path. Jordan, maybe call out how we handle audit logs?
01:24 Jordan: Right — the control plane will record route decisions and auth events; application-level prompts and responses are only logged if you enable the trace. For Dedicated we can restrict telemetry to your VPC and forward audit logs to your SIEM via our syslog/forwarder. I should flag that some service-level metrics (aggregated token counts, latencies) are kept for platform health but can be configured to be stripped of identifiers.
01:49 Tom: When you say 'strip identifiers' is that an automated redaction or manual? We need something compatible with our discovery process, e.g., legal hold.
01:58 Jordan: We have built-in redaction patterns and an API to register custom patterns; it's probabilistic so not perfect — I recommend we test with your example corpus. Also for legal hold you can ingest raw traces into your private storage if using Private deployment.
02:15 Priya: If we go hosted, who controls the keys? KMS residency is a blocker for us.
02:22 Maya: Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default, but we offer BYOK integration with customer KMS for Dedicated and Private. BYOK in Hosted is limited today. For Dedicated you can bring keys into a tenant-specific HSM via our customer-managed KMS flow.
02:40 Evan: Follow-up — does BYOK for Dedicated mean Redwood never has access to plaintext model inputs? What's the boundary?
02:47 Jordan: For Dedicated with customer KMS + VPC networking, plaintext inputs are processed on isolated worker pools. Redwood's control plane still orchestrates, but access to keys is gated; we can sign an operational runbook describing who in Redwood has emergency access. 
03:06 Sara: We will want that runbook and an escalation policy in the contract. Also, regarding audit logs, we need chain-of-custody evidence for e-discovery.
03:15 Maya: We can provide audit trails and an exportable evidence bundle, though the format varies by deployment. Jordan, can you add the export format to the follow-up?
03:23 Jordan: Yep, I'll add a sample export schema.
03:27 Tom: Performance question — if we pin a heavy hallucination guard prompt and enable caching, how much does that change latency? We're very sensitive for low-latency chat.
03:37 Jordan: There's a tradeoff: aggressive prefix and KV caching reduces token costs but can increase first-query latency for cache misses. We have batching and micro-batching controls. For low-latency routes we recommend small batch sizes and Dedicated capacity with reserved GPUs. We can run a short benchmark with your average sequence lengths.
03:56 Evan: On residency routing — we have subsidiaries in APAC and EMEA. Can we route specific customers to region-locked endpoints while still using a single tenancy?
04:06 Jordan: Yes, Smart Routing supports region policies by customer ID, route by latency or data residency tags. For strict data residency you might want tenant isolation (Dedicated or Private) so logs and KV caches never co-mingle.
04:20 Priya: And about log retention — our policy is 30 days for most telemetry, but records required for compliance can be kept up to seven years. We need the ability to set retention per log type and to freeze logs on legal hold.
04:33 Jordan: Retention is configurable by class in Dedicated/Private. Hosted lets you choose retention tiers but we manage the underlying storage. Legal hold support requires an administrative API that can freeze exports; that's available in Dedicated and Private today.
04:51 Sara: Is there a way to prove that logs were frozen and not tampered with? We need tamper-evidence for audits.
04:58 Jordan: We can hash and sign log bundles and provide the signature chain. For Private you can keep signing keys in your HSM.
05:09 Maya: Quick check — PCI scope? Any cardholder data touching model inputs?
05:13 Evan: A small fraction of our transaction support flow includes PAN-ish data in support transcripts. We're trying to scrub it before sending to LLMs, but want to assume the worst for mapping.
05:24 Priya: If PAN touches the model we will want a plan to keep that part of the product on-prem or in a fully isolated Dedicated instance and run attestation.
05:33 Jordan: For that we recommend Private deployment or a physically isolated Dedicated pool with strict network ACLs and SOC 2 plus PCI attestation. We have customers who run the most sensitive flows in Private on a co-lo or in their VPC.
05:45 Tom: On the encryption side — we heard about KMS escrow from other vendors. Do you support key escrow for regulatory scenarios?
05:52 Maya: We support custodian escrow patterns: you can register secondary key shares in a jurisdictional escrow if needed. We'll include the options in the matrix.
06:00 Evan: Another ask: redaction at-source, not later. We want an SDK-side scrub before it ever leaves our app servers. Is that possible?
06:08 Jordan: Absolutely. We provide client SDK libraries with pre-send hooks so you can run deterministic redactors or call out to an in-house scrubber. That way the string doesn't reach our network. We recommend deterministics for things like PAN regex and ML-based PII for names if you want to reduce residual risk.
06:26 Priya: About logs — we need separation between operational traces (latency/cost) and content traces (prompts/responses). Can we limit access to content traces to an allowlist of personnel?
06:38 Jordan: Yes, RBAC covers that. You can configure console roles where only people with X permission can retrieve content traces. For Dedicated/Private, access can be integrated with your SAML/SSO.
06:49 Sara: How do you handle subpoenas or government requests? Jurisdictional locking matters here.
06:56 Maya: We honor legal process for data under our custody. For Private deployments, Moonridge controls the data and would handle requests. For Hosted we have a process and would notify customers per contract terms; we can add notification SLAs.
07:10 Evan: We need a clean contract clause that says Redwood will notify within X hours and provide transparency; non-negotiable for us.
07:16 Sara: And we want a right to audit or a periodic audit report.
07:20 Jordan: We're SOC 2 Type II and can provide audit summaries; we also support customer-led audits for Private. Dedicated customers can request more frequent evidence packs.
07:31 Priya: Two technical questions before we close: first, are there any metadata leaks via model embeddings or vector stores? Second, do you support tenant-level index isolation?
07:42 Jordan: Embeddings can be kept tenant-specific; we don't shard or co-mingle vectors across tenants unless you enable multi-tenant indices. Isolation is recommended for regulated data; we also have encryption at rest for vector stores and per-tenant keying. There is a risk model for embedding leakage if you query shared indices — we'll run auditing to estimate it.
07:59 Tom: For our pilot, we want to run a small set of traffic that includes simulated PII and measure what shows up in logs and what needs redaction.
08:07 Maya: That's doable — Jordan will craft a pilot plan. We'll need your sample inputs and the list of endpoints you'd like to test.
08:15 Evan: Timeline — we want to decide hosting approach by end of October, pilot in November, production early Q1.
08:23 Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get the comparison matrix and runbook out by the 14th.
08:28 Sara: One more legal note — cross-border transfer clauses. We need to see template clauses for subprocessors.
08:34 Maya: We'll include subprocessors and subprocess locations in the doc.
08:39 Priya: Anything else on the security checklist? I also want to know about network egress controls and the ability to restrict outbound to only your model endpoints.
08:49 Jordan: You can lock egress via VPC peering and outbound ACLs on Dedicated/Private. Hosted is more limited — we can filter conversations but not the low-level network egress on your side.
09:00 Evan: Ok thanks everyone. Quick recap?
09:05 Maya: Recap: (1) We'll send hosting comparison + KMS/escrow options + SOC/PCI summaries; (2) Jordan will prepare pilot runbook and sample telemetry export; (3) Moonridge will share infra diagram, privacy checklist, and sample inputs. Target sign-offs and pilot scheduling as per next steps.
09:26 Priya: Good. I'll follow up with the compliance doc. Thanks.
09:30 Meeting end.
